by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the property is held for personal rather than business use.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently as the any-other-property alternative, including when apparel, a motor vehicle, or a prescribed health aid also has a specific exemption. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, and (e) covers professionally prescribed health aids. A value above a limit does not eliminate either applicable alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use § 12-1001(d) for ordinary household property; it requires implements, professional books, or tools of the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel under subsection (a), and do not omit subsection (b) merely because a specific subsection applies.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the debtor owns personal-use property.
by_task.procedure: Determine eligibility before calculating amounts. Independently include § 12-1001(b) for any debtor-owned personal-use property, including property also covered by subsection (a), (c), or (e); a value above its ceiling does not defeat eligibility. Use the lesser of value and $4,000 for one debtor or $8,000 for jointly owned property of two debtors. For a motor vehicle, also report subsection (c) at the lesser of value and $2,400, without doubling that limit. Sections (a) and (e) use the asset value because the supplied text states no dollar ceiling.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use subsection (d) merely because an item could be called a tool or implement; require facts showing use in the debtor's trade. Do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel, omit subsection (b) because a specific subsection applies, treat either ceiling as an eligibility test, or apply these exemptions to business-use property.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the debtor owns personal property, including property expressly identified as a tool of the debtor's trade.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for every item of personal property, including when subsection (a), (c), (d), or (e) also applies. Section (a) covers necessary wearing apparel, (c) covers a motor vehicle, (d) covers an implement, professional book, or tool expressly used in the debtor's trade, and (e) covers a professionally prescribed health aid. A value above a limit does not eliminate an applicable alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property. Do not classify jewelry or a watch as necessary wearing apparel, or a device that displays pictures as a family picture. Require express trade-use facts for subsection (d), and do not classify business machinery as a motor vehicle merely because it can move.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the debtor owns personal property or an occupied homestead.
by_task.procedure: Determine eligibility before amounts. For every item of personal property, report § 12-1001(b) independently at the lesser of value and $4,000 for one debtor or $8,000 for jointly owned property of two debtors, including an expressly identified trade tool and property also covered by (a), (c), (d), or (e). Report subsection (c) for a motor vehicle at the lesser of value and $2,400 without doubling. Report subsection (d) for an expressly identified trade tool at the lesser of value and $1,500 for one debtor or $3,000 for jointly owned property of two debtors. Subsections (a) and (e) use asset value. For an equal-half jointly owned occupied homestead, § 12-901 gives a $15,000 proportionate-share claim, not one combined $30,000 claim.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply personal-property subsections to real property, including burial realty or a homestead. Do not use subsection (d) without express trade-use facts, subsection (c) for business machinery that is not a motor vehicle, or subsection (a) for jewelry, a watch, or a device merely capable of displaying family pictures. Do not treat any dollar ceiling as an eligibility test.
